subject: [PATCH v4 0/4] mm: split underused anonymous mTHP folios

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the sysctl value is rarely modified during application runtime, and suggested this as a justification for hard-coding the minimum folio size in patch 4.
reviews.raw_body:
This sounds reasonable. In production, as far as I know from speaking with folks
in conferences, no one changes the value during application runtime
(atleast this is true in meta). Its usually only changed before the workload
starts (or just at boot time).

Acked-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer requested a minor change to the commit by asking to replace 'THP' with 'PMD mapped THP' in the thp_underused_split_page section of /proc/vmstat, and gave an LGTM (Looks Good To Me) approval.
reviews.raw_body:
In this same commit, would you mind also doing s/THP/PMD mapped THP/ in
thp_underused_split_page section in /proc/vmstat section?

Apart from that, LGTM

Acked-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

2026-11-03.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory regressions caused by 2M THP=always on arm64 by allowing the underused shrinker to handle anonymous mTHP folios. The patches modify thp_underused() to be folio-size-aware, stop queueing folios for underused splitting when khugepaged/max_ptes_none is at its default maximum, and add a per-order split_underused counter. Finally, it queues anonymous mTHP folios on the deferred split list with a minimum size of 2M.

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Barry Song expressed agreement with the hardcoded 2M minimum folio size for mTHP folios, which was previously discussed and agreed upon.
reviews.raw_body:
I believe we discussed this before and agreed that a
hardcoded 2MB would be a better starting point.

Reviewed-by: Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org>
